newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Amcor starts paper anti-dumping action.
newsitem.headline: Amcor starts paper anti-dumping action.

text.p: Paper manufacturer Amcor Ltd said on Thursday its printing and writing papers unit Australian Paper had commenced anti-dumping action against 14 countries which it considers are dumping paper in Australia.
Australian Paper said the product which it believes is being dumped is two-sided coated woodfree paper sheets between 75 to 150 grammage mainly used by magazines, brochures and posters.

Arthur Williamson, Australian Paper's general manager sales and marketing, told Reuters the average spot price for this paper had collapsed to between A$1,350 to A$1,340 per tonnes from A$1,950 per tonne earlier this year.

"We have had to go down to match those prices. We are making losses at those prices and I know that all the overseas countries that are putting product into this market are not making profits," Williamson said.
Williamson said the countries involved were South Korea, Japan, Italy, Finland, Indonesia, South Africa, Taiwan, Germany, France, Sweden, Austria, Belgium, Switzerland and the Netherlands.

Australian law allows local manufacturers affected by dumping to seek remedies in the form of anti-dumping and countervailing duties in each country which lifts importers' prices to those charged in their home market.
Australian Paper's share of this coated paper market in Australia is 20 percent with the remaining 80 percent imported.

Williamson said South Korea and Indonesia were seen as the most agressive of the importers with South Korea having grown their share of this market to more than 30 percent from less than 10 percent within a year.
"There has been a major supply balance change taking place in the market," he said.
Australia has a five percent tariff on paper and no indirect tariffs compared to many Asian countries which have direct tariffs of up to 20 percent as well as indirect tariffs.
